* feat(hy_v4_vl): add open-source HY4-VL model

Add the HY4-VL (Hunyuan V4 Vision-Language) model to Transformers:
modular/modeling code, configuration, image & video processors (torch and
PIL variants), processor, auto mappings and conversion mapping, plus model
documentation and tests.

- inherit the Qwen2-VL top level and reuse the framework RoPE layout and
  tensor-parallel sinks, dropping most model-specific overrides
- match the released checkpoint numerics
- register the model in the auto classes, models __init__ and toctree

* refactor(hy_v4_vl): keep TP sinks model-local, support cached encoder outputs

- drop the framework-level `colwise_local` TP style; shard attention sinks
  with plain `colwise` and convert them to a local tensor inside the eager
  attention path instead
- rename the attention layer type to `indexed_attention`
- accept `mm_encoder_outputs` in `forward` and expand cached visual features
  per sample (instead of per image) when generation expands the batch
- image/video processors: copy the default `size` instead of mutating it,
  deprecate call-time `min_pixels`/`max_pixels` in favor of `size`
- tests: sharded-sinks forward/backward, eager attention without sinks,
  RGB conversion before preprocess, size override handling

* refactor(hy_v4_vl): share the vision patch merger with hunyuan_vl

- split HunYuanVLVisionPatchMerger.forward into `_reshape_features` and
  `_postprocess_features` hooks, keeping the shared projection and the
  newline/begin/end tokens in the parent
- make HYV4VLVisionPatchMerger inherit it and override the two hooks for
  its per-frame merge; alias `before_rms` to the existing `norm` so the
  released checkpoints keep loading
- rename `act` to `proj_act` to match the parent's naming
- tests: projection and boundary tokens, spatial checks, conv reference,
  and unused parameters stay gradient-free

* refactor(hy_v4_vl): apply community review on the PR base (#34)

Port the community review changes without bringing unrelated upstream history into the PR. Retain model-local packed generation and test adaptations required by the existing base, and expose router outputs through local recording hooks.

Simplify configuration and processor APIs, use checkpoint key conversion for before_rms, and regenerate the models against the pinned base. Validate CUDA regression tests, real vision feature parity, tensor-parallel gradients, and complete text, image, and video generation outputs.

declared as empty subclasses in the modular file, so the generated files
hold a full, in-sync copy of the parent implementation, the same way
hunyuan_vl relates to qwen2_vl. This keeps checkpoints that record

checkpoints that record HunYuanVLImageProcessor keep working.

being ignored, and frames are never upscaled beyond their input

signature, so reusing that name would bind the image classes to the video

Granite for Docling (#49012)

* feat: add GraniteForDocling

Add the GraniteForDocling vision-language model for document conversion.
Pages are tiled at 512x512 with a pixel-shuffle connector, DeepStack
injection of intermediate vision features, and a dense Granite-style
text decoder that generates DocLang.

The same modeling code loads different GraniteForDocling sizes and
configurations via text_config and vision_config, and different
projectors (high-resolution or density router). The fine path can be
selected per request with fine_route=True; checkpoints trained with the
coarse path only set use_fine_route=False and do not build it. Optional
multi-token prediction heads (num_mtp_layers) add an auxiliary training
loss. Serving engines such as vLLM can use the same heads as draft heads
for speculative decoding; generate does not.

The model is written as a modular file; the configuration, image
processors (torchvision and PIL backends), processor and modeling files
are generated from it. The image processors tile pages on the grid
closest to their aspect ratio, capped at 16 tiles per side to match the
tokenizer's tile position markers, and pad batches on the tile dimension.

Regenerate the standalone model and processor from the modular source and add regression coverage. The per-call image_seq_len override remains a documented known issue.

* docs: drop redundant dtype/attn_implementation and padding_side tips

Review feedback: the config already sets the dtype and sdpa is the default;
padding_side=left ships in the checkpoint's tokenizer config instead.

* Address review: vision model owns the connector, standard Granite MLP, no MTP module

- The multi-token prediction heads are no longer built or loaded by transformers

* Fix Mask2Former _init_weights to match Meta's original initialization

Fix three initialization bugs where _init_weights diverged from Meta's
original Mask2Former code:

1. nn.Embedding layers received normal_(std=0.02) from the base

   Meta's original _reset_parameters only applies xavier_uniform_ on
   tensors where p.dim() > 1, leaving biases at PyTorch's default
   Kaiming uniform. Now handled by a dedicated Mask2FormerPredictionBlock

   normal_(std=0), effectively zeroing it. Meta's original does not
   explicitly initialize level_embed. Changed to normal_(std=1.0).

Moved super()._init_weights() from a blanket call at the top to an
else branch, so it only runs for modules not handled by
Mask2Former-specific logic. Uses transformers.initialization helpers
throughout.

embedding std, MLP biases, level_embed, and deformable attention init.

use plain strings. The registry lookup splits into `get_export_config_class` and

Exporters: ONNX Runtime fusions at export time (`OnnxConfig(ort_fusions=...)`) (#50309)

* Exporters: feed SDPA's boolean mask to ONNX as an additive one

torchlib guards its boolean-mask softmax with an IsNaN/Where over the whole
(query, key) weight matrix; the patch already zeroes fully masked rows, so the
guard only costs time (2x on a 2520-patch vision attention on ORT CPU).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Exporters: fuse ONNX exports into ONNX Runtime's ops at export time

`OnnxConfig(ort_fusions="cpu" | "cuda")` fuses the exported graph into ONNX Runtime's
transformer ops before it is quantized and saved: RMS / layer / skip norms, rotary
embeddings, MultiHeadAttention, GroupQueryAttention over the key-value cache (rotating
itself), MoE (CUDA), and packed sibling projections. onnxscript's `optimize_for_ort`
does the core fusions; `onnxruntime_fusions.py` prepares the graph for them, repairs
the ones ONNX Runtime rejects or miscomputes, and adds the rest. Off by default
(`None`): the fused ops aren't standard ONNX.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Exporters: explain the ORT fusion tests, plainer docs

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Exporters: grouped_mm without Slices; fuse float16 MoE blocks

The grouped_mm translation takes each group's end and weights from one Split and gathers
its rows from a Range: onnxscript's SlicesSplit rule tries every pair of Slices in the
graph, and a Slice per expert and layer made it most of an MoE export's time (granite
1B-A400M: export 23 min -> 5 min, an ORT fusion pass 13 min -> 2 min).

The MoE fusion steps over the casts a float16 model's router and expert sum compute
through in float32, so real checkpoints fuse, not only float32 ones.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Exporters: on CPU, unfuse the attentions GroupQueryAttention didn't take

ONNX Runtime's CPU MultiHeadAttention with an attention bias runs slower than the
MatMuls and Softmax it fuses (2.5x on Qwen3-0.6B's decode step), so for
`ort_fusions="cpu"` the ones left after the GroupQueryAttention fusion (encoders,
attention without a cache) go back to plain ops. EmbeddingGemma2 on CPU: 0.98x -> 1.17x.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Exporters: ORT fusions on ONNX Runtime 1.29

- Graphs fused for "cuda" need onnxruntime>=1.27 (fp32 accumulation in the
  CUDA skip norms, microsoft/onnxruntime#28682): the fp16 skip-norm unfusing
  is dropped, with a warning when an older version is installed.
- GroupQueryAttention: a known total length goes in as an int32 constant
  (1.29's shape inference reads one computed from shapes as int64), and a
  decode taking any number of tokens is fused only for a batch of one (1.29
  rejects several new tokens after a past for a larger batch). It's a CPU-only
  step: CUDA's rejects the bias every masked attention has.
- MoE: SiLU-gated experts only; 1.29's CUDA MoE miscomputes gated GELU.
- The pipeline is a `(name, step, providers)` table.
- The export tests fuse for the provider they run on (`torch_device`).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Exporters: trace MoE experts as batched_mm for CUDA fusions

With `ort_fusions="cuda"`, the ONNX exporter traces mixture-of-experts layers
with `batched_mm` (restoring the model's own implementation after), and the
`MoE` fusion matches that form: each routed row's expert weight picked by
`GatherND`, a batched `MatMul`, the SiLU gate, the weighted sum per token.
Its graph is a fraction of `grouped_mm`'s per-expert one, so Granite 3.0
1B-A400M exports in 69 s instead of 302 s and fuses in 15 s instead of 130 s,
to the same `MoE` graph. `"cpu"` and unfused exports keep `grouped_mm`, whose
prefill stays fast unfused. A warning says when a block doesn't fuse.

* Exporters: GroupQueryAttention on CUDA for decode with a dynamic cache

On ONNX Runtime 1.29, CUDA's `GroupQueryAttention` takes the attention bias
and is exact. It's a large win for decode (Qwen3-0.6B: 7.48 -> 4.71 ms,
3.71x with a CUDA graph) but slower than `MultiHeadAttention` for a prefill,
and a static cache's total length, computed on the GPU, is read as 0
(microsoft/onnxruntime#33867). So "cuda" fuses decode steps over a dynamic
cache only; "cpu" fuses every case as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Exporters: CUDA GroupQueryAttention for static caches too

A static cache attends over its whole buffer: `total_sequence_length` is the
buffer's length as an int32 constant, the bias spans the buffer (the cache's
mask already masks the slots not written), and `seqlens_k` carries each
sequence's written length. A constant never lives on the GPU, which CUDA's
kernel reads as 0 (microsoft/onnxruntime#33867), so static caches fuse on
CUDA too. CUDA's step stays decode-only: with a bias, its prefill runs an
unfused kernel, slower than `MultiHeadAttention`'s.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Exporters: GroupQueryAttention over transformers' folded decode attention

Since #49743, a single-token SDPA step without `enable_gqa` folds the query heads
onto their key-value heads (`[batch, kv_heads, groups, head_dim]`) instead of
repeating the keys and values, which onnxscript fuses into a `MultiHeadAttention`
over the key-value heads. The `GroupQueryAttention` fusion reads that form too:
the query heads behind the fold, the bias behind its expand over the group rows,
`num_heads` the key-value heads times the groups, its output reshaped back to
the folded layout.

provider alone. The zero rows are appended with a `Concat` instead.

OpenVINO exporter: let OpenVINO fuse attention, RoPE, the KV cache and compressed matmuls (#50311)

* OpenVINO exporter: repeat GQA heads with `repeat_kv` so OpenVINO fuses its KV-cache attention

The exporter swapped `repeat_kv` for `repeat_interleave`, and its SDPA patch repeated
K/V the same way. `repeat_interleave` lowers to a `Gather` between the stateful KV
cache and the attention, which OpenVINO's CPU plugin can't fuse: every attention ran
decomposed into MatMul/Softmax and copied the cache each step. Keep transformers'
`repeat_kv` (unsqueeze, expand, reshape) in both places.

The frozen KV length the `repeat_kv` patch worked around no longer reproduces on
OpenVINO 2026.4: Qwen2.5-0.5B and Qwen3-0.6B decode a left-padded batch of two, 48
tokens past the prompt, token-for-token like eager.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* OpenVINO exporter: drop the SDPA patch's fully-masked-row zeroing

The patch zeroed the attention output of rows that mask every key, with a select on a
mask-derived condition after each SDPA. OpenVINO's CPU plugin miscomputes that pattern:
EmbeddingGemma2's fp32 export returned NaN (layer 2 onwards) with no row fully masked.
Without it the fp32 export matches eager (token cosine 1.0000), and a fully masked row
gets the uniform average its dtype-minimum mask describes, as transformers' eager
attention gives it. Generated tokens are unaffected: Qwen2.5-0.5B and Qwen3-0.6B still
decode a left-padded batch of two like eager.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* OpenVINO exporter: trace bf16/fp16 models as f32 graphs

OpenVINO's CPU plugin fuses its kernels on f32-typed graphs and picks the inference
precision itself (bf16 on CPUs with AMX or AVX-512 BF16). A bf16-typed graph misses
some of them, notably the compressed-weight matmuls of an NNCF int8/int4 graph:
every weight was decompressed on each call. Trace and convert in f32, then give each
parameter and buffer, and each config, its own dtype back. With an f32 inference hint
the f32 graph matches eager f32 on the same weights token for token.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* OpenVINO exporter: give KV-cache variables the update's dims instead of reshaping the update

A batch-1 sample specializes the batch of the cache concat to 1 while its variable stays batch-dynamic, so
`_pin_state_update_shapes` put a Reshape between the concat and its `Assign`. That Reshape keeps the CPU
plugin from fusing the cache into its stateful SDPA. The variable now takes the dims the update fixes, and a
pinning Reshape is only added where the variable fixes a dim the update leaves dynamic.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* OpenVINO exporter: fold the frontend's marked scalar casts so RoPE fuses

The PyTorch frontend translates `aten.neg` as a multiply by a `Convert`ed -1, with the Convert marked
DisableConstantFolding and the multiply marked as a dequantization node. Until those marks are dropped,
which only happens on serialization, the CPU plugin's RoPE fusion doesn't match `rotate_half`. Fold such scalar
Converts into constants and drop the marks on their consumers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* OpenVINO exporter: store a 16-bit model's weights as 16-bit constants plus a Convert

After the f32 trace, restore bf16/fp16 weights as 16-bit constants followed by a Convert to f32. The CPU plugin
decompresses this pattern inside its FullyConnected, and the IR keeps the checkpoint's exact values at their
original size.

commits.message:
Fold GQA query heads onto their KV head when decoding instead of repeating K/V (#49743)

* [`SDPA`] Fold GQA query heads onto their KV head when decoding

When `use_gqa_in_sdpa` is False (on CUDA and CPU: every call with a mask, so
every decoding step of left-padded batched generation), `sdpa_attention_forward`
copied K/V `num_key_value_groups` times with `repeat_kv` in every layer at every
step, a cost that grows with the context length.

With a single query token, pass the query heads that share a KV head as query
rows of that head instead: (batch, num_heads, 1, head_dim) ->
(batch, num_kv_heads, num_key_value_groups, head_dim). The head mapping is the
same as `repeat_kv`, a mask shared by all heads broadcasts over the new rows (a
per-head mask, e.g. from `position_bias`, is folded the same way), and SDPA runs
plain multi-head attention on the same fused kernel without copying K/V.

commits.message:
Restore BLT's 512-byte sliding windows (entropy patcher + local encoder/decoder) (#49188)

* Fix BLT entropy patcher missing its 512-token sliding window

`BltPatcher` scored the entropy model with an unbounded causal mask, but BLT's
entropy model is specified with a local block-causal bias over a 512-token
sliding window. Without the window the predicted entropies are systematically
inflated, so far more bytes clear `patching_threshold` and the patch rate
collapses on inputs longer than the window: 1.15 bytes/patch instead of 4.07 on
held-out DCLM, i.e. ~3.5x more latent positions than BLT is designed to run at.
Inputs <= 512 bytes are unaffected, which is what makes it easy to miss.

The released checkpoints already declare the intent: `facebook/blt-entropy`
carries `attn_bias_type: "local_block_causal"` and `sliding_window: 512`, and
`itazap/blt-1b-hf`'s `patcher_config` even ships `attn_bias_type:
"local_block_causal"` -- nothing read it.

- add `sliding_window` to `BltPatcherConfig` (default 512, so already-published
  checkpoints are fixed without a config change)
- dispatch to `create_sliding_window_causal_mask` in `BltPatcher.forward`
- stop dropping `sliding_window` in the weight conversion script

Verified against `itazap/blt-1b-hf` on 24 wikitext-2 documents; bytes/patch
before -> after: 256 B 3.03 -> 3.03, 512 B 3.37 -> 3.36, 1024 B 1.77 -> 3.48,
2048 B 1.29 -> 3.64, 3840 B 1.15 -> 3.72. The windowed numbers reproduce
`facebookresearch/blt` on the same bytes (4.0716 vs 4.0710 bytes/patch on the
320-window DCLM set).

Fixes #49185

* Also restore BLT's 512-byte local attention window

The first commit only fixed the entropy patcher. BLT applies a 512-byte window in three
places, and the released checkpoints declare all of them:

  entropy model        attn_bias_type=local_block_causal, sliding_window=512
  local enc / decoder  local_attention_window_len=512
  global transformer   block_causal (no window)

`facebook/blt-1b`'s config carries `local_attention_window_len: 512`, but the conversion
dropped it and `BltConfig` had nowhere to put it, so the byte-level mask shared by the local
encoder and decoder was built full-causal. Restoring only the entropy window is not enough:
on S-NIAH the port scores 0.47 with no window and 0.12 with the entropy window alone,
against 0.96 with all three (official bytelatent: 0.963).

- add `local_attention_window_len` to `BltConfig` (default 512)
- `BltModel.forward` builds the byte-level mask with `create_sliding_window_causal_mask`
  when it is set; the global patch-level mask stays causal
- carry `local_attention_window_len` through the weight conversion script

Verified equivalent to a known-good reference implementation of the same fix: identical
logits on `itazap/blt-1b-hf` at 400, 1200 and 3000 byte inputs (logit sums -744560.875 /
-2255387.25 / -5830551.0, matching last-position argmax).

* Drop explanatory comments from BLT sliding-window masks

* BLT: build byte-level sliding mask from encoder_config instead of copying config

* BLT: read local_attention_window_len in BltModel.forward

check_config_attributes flagged BltConfig.local_attention_window_len as unused
because only its copy in encoder_config.sliding_window was read. Choosing the
byte-level mask from local_attention_window_len also makes setting it to None
after loading restore full causal attention.

* Add BLT sliding-window regression tests

- config defaults (512) and save/reload of patcher_config.sliding_window and
  local_attention_window_len
- entropy patcher: entropies past the window do not depend on bytes outside it
- local encoder/decoder: outputs match full causal within the window and
  differ beyond it

* fix(fetcher): case-sensitive submodule check on case-insensitive filesystems

commits.message:
perf(ci): skip the lazy blob fetch in `git blame` on a partial clone (#50007)

`check_noisy_comments.py` runs `git blame --line-porcelain` per file that has
findings, to decide whether a comment is old enough to ignore and whether the
file's owner wrote it. On a partial clone (`git clone --filter=blob:none`,
routine for a repo this size) the historical blobs blame needs are not on disk,
so plain `git blame` lazily fetches each missing object from the promisor remote
-- one object at a time, inside git's own machinery. Each round trip is slow even
when it ultimately fails: measured here at ~12s per file, and 97-138s for files
with long histories (`masking_utils.py`, `conversion_mapping.py`).

On this checkout's default diff-only scan (56 files with findings) that added up
to 52m48s of wall time for a check whose actual comment parsing takes ~4s.

Setting `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` for this one subprocess makes a missing object a
local, immediate failure instead of a network fetch. `blame` already reports
that as a nonzero exit, which the caller treats as "no blame info for this
file", so behavior is unchanged where every object is local -- the ordinary
case in CI, where actions/checkout makes a full clone. Where the flag does
trigger, the cutoff/owner filters simply see no commit dates, which can only
keep a finding, never hide one.

Measured on the default diff-only path: 52m48s -> ~1m48s (~29x).

Adds a regression test asserting the env var reaches the subprocess; it fails
without the fix.

commits.message:
Install the TP gradient all-reduce only when grad is enabled (#49975)

`ReplicatedWithGradAllReduce.install_forward` registered a module-level
backward hook on every per-head norm at TP setup time. Dynamo breaks the
graph at each call of a module carrying a full backward hook, including
under `torch.no_grad()`, so `tp_plan="auto"` cost every affected model a
graph break per norm per layer in inference. Reported for Qwen3, where
decoding slowed from 37.6 ms to 140 ms per token.

Register the all-reduce from the module's forward instead, and only when
`torch.is_grad_enabled()`: inference installs nothing. Doing it at forward
time rather than install time also means the parameters the loader actually
installed are the ones hooked, which is what the module-level hook was
working around, so a `register_post_accumulate_grad_hook` is safe here.

That also removes a latent bug. A full backward hook fires on grad w.r.t.
outputs when no input requires grad, at which point `param.grad` is still
None and the all-reduce was silently skipped; a post-accumulate hook cannot
run before the gradient exists.

* Respect CSM codebook embedding tying configuration

`CsmConfig` unconditionally set `tie_word_embeddings = False`, so the core
`get_expanded_tied_weights_keys` dropped CSM's structural tie between the
backbone audio embeddings and the depth decoder embeddings. They then loaded

instead, since both flags have the same meaning for CSM. Older checkpoints

🚨Add an FP8 backend to `QuantizedCache` (#48677)

* Add an FP8 backend to `QuantizedCache`

* Reorder the FP8 states for beam search

* Use an early return in `Fp8QuantizedLayer.reorder_cache`

* Measure the quantized cache backends accurately

The memory of the quantized states was under-reported: only `fp8` stores
them as a plain tensor, `hqq` uses a `(tensor, metadata)` tuple and quanto
a tensor subclass whose payload sits in its attributes, neither of which
`numel() * element_size()` accounts for.

Also report the KL divergence of the next-token distribution against the
bf16 one, as the matching token count saturates on short generations, and
copy the `cache_config` per call, which `generate` consumes.

* Reset the FP8 scales, and cover the FP8 backend in the quantized layer tests

* Address review on the FP8 quantized cache layer

- `fp8_max` becomes a class attribute next to `fp8_dtype`, instead of being
  recomputed and stored on every instance. This matches how the FP8 constants
  are already defined in `integrations/finegrained_fp8.py` and
  `integrations/compressed_tensors.py`.

- `Fp8QuantizedLayer` now overrides `lazy_initialization` to calibrate the
  scales, rather than doing it inline in the first `update` call.

- `_quantized_keys` and `_quantized_values` are initialized to `None` in
  `QuantizedLayer.__init__`, so that they are always defined before the first
  `update`. This was missing for the quanto and hqq layers as well.

- `.contiguous()` is now only called in `lazy_initialization`. The states
  passed to `update` come straight from a transpose in the attention layer, so
  they are genuinely non-contiguous during prefill, and `_quantize` propagates
  that layout. Every subsequent append goes through a `cat`, whose output is
  contiguous by construction, so the call is redundant there.

- `_cat_fp8` is removed in favour of a plain `torch.cat`, which handles
  `float8_e4m3fn` natively on CPU and CUDA, for contiguous and non-contiguous
  inputs alike (checked on torch 2.8 through 2.14).

* Trim the comments down to one line

* Store the FP8 scale alongside the states it quantizes

`_quantize` already returned a `(states, scale)` pair, but the two halves were
then split across `_quantized_keys` and a separate `_key_scale` attribute, and
zipped back together at every `_dequantize` call site.

Keeping the pair as the layer's single quantized payload matches what
`HQQQuantizedLayer` does with `(qtensor, meta)`, lets `_dequantize` be called on
`_quantized_keys` directly like the base class does, and removes the `reset`
override, since `QuantizedLayer.reset` already drops `_quantized_keys`.

It also keeps the scale's rank internal to `_quantize` / `_dequantize`, so a
future per-block backend can make it a tensor without changing the layer's
attributes.

* Say what the `.contiguous()` in `lazy_initialization` is actually for

Nothing in `_quantize` needs a contiguous input: on strided states it computes
the same scale and gives bit-identical dequantized values.

What the call is for is the layout of the stored buffer. The states handed to
`lazy_initialization` come from a transpose in the attention layer, while the
ones `update` appends come out of `cat`, and the two disagree: without the call
the buffer is laid out as `[B, S, H, D]` after the prefill and as `[B, H, S, D]`
from the first decode step on. Normalizing it once keeps the strides the same
for the buffer's whole life, which matters for the follow-up feeding these
states to FP8 attention kernels.

The test was building its states with `torch.randn(1, 2, 5, 8)`, so they were
already contiguous and the assertion held whether or not the call was there. It
now builds them the way the attention layer does.

* Address @vasqu's review

Drop the benchmark script: it belongs in the PR description rather than in the
code base.

Drop the `.contiguous()` in `lazy_initialization`. Nothing in `_quantize` needs
it, and nothing reads the quantized states while they are still strided, so the
layout only matters once something actually consumes the FP8 buffer. Better
added then, with a consumer to justify it.

Trim the class docstring down to what is specific to this backend, and the
`_quantize` and `reorder_cache` ones down to one point each.

The test now builds its states the way the attention layer does, so the strided
path is covered.

* One-line the docstrings and comments that fit on one line

* Keep the FP8 state initialization out of the shared quantized layer

* Split the quantized layer into a base and a group-wise class

The group-wise options only belong to the integer backends, so they move to
`GroupWiseQuantizedLayer` and `Fp8QuantizedLayer` no longer inherits them.
`QuantizedCache` now rejects them for the `fp8` backend instead of silently
replacing them.

* Note which subtree a future fp8 variation belongs to

Grouping along the head dimension keeps the states appendable, so it has no
use for the residual window `GroupWiseQuantizedLayer` exists for.

* Keep the group-wise signature on QuantizedLayer and name the new base

The split moved the group-wise options out of QuantizedLayer, which breaks
subclasses that pass them to super().__init__. Keep that signature where it
was and introduce BaseQuantizedLayer for what the backends share instead.

The vibevoice guard now skips on the new base, so FP8 layers keep being
skipped there.

* Declare the quantized states in the base layer, and group the quantized tests

The states were only assigned in `reset` and `lazy_initialization`, so a freshly
built layer had no such attribute at all.

The FP8 tests move next to the other quantized ones, and the beam reordering and
reset tests are parameterized over the backends instead of duplicated.

GradiumPhononTTS: Pocket TTS trained by Gradium. Differences, all in the modular file:
the voice prompt is made of 512-dim speaker-codec latents (`audio_prompt_dim`), a
learnt speaker vector is added to every audio latent (`embed_audio_latents`), no voice

(nemotron3_5_asr precedent, TRF009 allowlist). Conversion, the normalising chat
